root_cause.text: In `net/bluetooth/hci_event.c`, `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()` walks BT_BOUND BIS connections with an unbounded `while` loop and uses `ev->bis_handle[i++]` before verifying `i < ev->num_bis`, so a malformed `LE_Create_BIG_Complete` event can trigger an out-of-bounds read and leave connections in BT_BOUND state, causing the same entry to be revisited indefinitely under `hci_dev_lock`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ev->num_bis <= i) { ... hci_conn_del(conn); continue; }` immediately before accessing `ev->bis_handle[i++]`, and also forces BIG termination when `hci_conn_set_handle()` fails or when not all BISes were connected, matching the commit/CVE description that the old code could read past the flex array and loop forever.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add error handling for missing BIS handles and handle-assignment failures during BIG creation to abort incomplete BIG setup cleanly.
intent_record.what: In hci_le_create_big_complete_evt(), a new bounds check was added before reading ev->bis_handle[i] to ensure ev->num_bis is greater than the current index; if not, the code now logs an error, sets ev->status to HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED, confirms the connection with that error, deletes the connection, and continues. The existing hci_conn_set_handle() call was also changed to check its return value; on failure it now logs an error, forces the same error status, confirms and deletes the connection, and then continues.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from using an unavailable BIS handle entry and from proceeding with a connection whose handle could not be assigned. In both failure cases, the BIG creation sequence is terminated as unsuccessful by propagating an unspecified HCI error, which avoids leaving partially connected BIS links and ensures the BIG is torn down when not all BIS can be connected.

intent_record.intent_summary: Terminate the BIG when creation fails with an unspecified error or when no BIS connections were established.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding BIG termination in `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()` was changed from `if (!ev->status && !i)` to `if (ev->status == HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED || (!ev->status && !i))`, and a comment was added explaining that an unexpected error or no connected BISes should cause the BIG to be terminated.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now also terminates the BIG when the completion status reports `HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED`, not only when the BIG creation succeeds but no BIS connections were established. This prevents a BIG from lingering in an invalid or incomplete state after an unexpected error.

grouping_result.intent: Terminate the BIG when creation fails with an unspecified error or when no BIS connections were established.

consistency_review.core_intent: Abort incomplete BIG setup by terminating BIG creation when BIS handles are missing, assignments fail, or creation ends without establishing BIS connections.

relevance_review.reason: The changes target LE BIG completion/setup error handling for incomplete or malformed BIG creation, which is directly related to the vulnerable path in hci_le_create_big_complete_evt() where BIS handling can go wrong and leave BT_BOUND entries uncleared. While the summary does not explicitly mention the out-of-bounds read, it addresses the same BIG/BIS completion logic and the failure mode that can lead to the bug.

candidates.rationale: This expression increments i and dereferences ev->bis_handle before any bounds check against ev->num_bis, which matches the root cause of an out-of-bounds read when a malformed LE_Create_BIG_Complete event advertises fewer BIS handles than the loop consumes.

This is the loop continuation taken after failed handle assignment; in the vulnerable flow, the loop keeps iterating over BT_BOUND BIS connections without enforcing a stop when event data is exhausted, contributing to the unbounded traversal under hci_dev_lock.

This condition shows the pre-fix logic only checked whether any BISes were connected after processing, but did not prevent the earlier out-of-bounds access or infinite revisiting of bound connections when the event data was malformed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This exact expression consumes ev->bis_handle with i++ before any check against ev->num_bis, which is the out-of-bounds read described in the root cause when a malformed LE_Create_BIG_Complete event provides too few BIS handles.

This loop continuation is part of the pre-fix control flow that keeps walking BT_BOUND BIS connections even after handle-assignment failure, allowing repeated revisiting under hci_dev_lock when the event data is exhausted.

This condition reflects the incomplete pre-fix termination logic: it only checks whether any BISes were established after processing, but does not stop the earlier unsafe iteration or prevent the malformed-event out-of-bounds access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this version of `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()`. The patch replaces the old single-lookup logic with `list_for_each_entry_rcu(conn, &hdev->conn_hash.list, list)` and uses `conn->handle = __le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[bis_idx++]);` only while iterating BIS-bound connections. In addition, this commit adds a guard for the no-BIS case: `if (!ev->status && !bis_idx) ... hci_le_terminate_big_sync(...)`, which addresses the case where no BISes were connected. The old bug pattern was an unbounded loop / out-of-bounds access on `ev->bis_handle[i++]` before verifying bounds; that exact flawed logic is no longer shown here. Since the code already contains the multi-BIS handling and the termination fallback, this snippet reflects the fixed implementation rather than the bug.
